GlobeNewswire — "Reco Raises $55 Million in Additional Funding with Participation from AT&T Ventures"

item.title: Is Instinct Worth $10B? Inside the $1B Series C
item.dc:creator: YourInfoDaily
item.description: Instinct raised $1B in Series C funding from Sequoia, Benchmark and Coatue at a $10B valuation for a personal AI agent that handles everyday tasks end to end.
item.content:encoded:
Sequoia, Benchmark and Coatue back a product still in early access, betting on agents that finish tasks rather than answer questions.

Instinct, a San Francisco company building a personal AI agent, has raised $1 billion in a Series C from Sequoia Capital, Benchmark and Coatue at a $10 billion valuation.

The company was founded by Noah Shinn.

An Agent With Its Own Phone

Instinct is pitched as a personal agent rather than a chatbot. It handles everyday errands, planning a trip, ordering groceries, canceling a subscription, using its own phone and computer access to carry tasks through to completion.

The distinction matters. Most consumer AI products answer questions and hand the work back. An agent that holds its own accounts and devices can finish the job, which also means it needs far more trust from the person it works for.

"We're building Instinct to be the best personal agent that can handle the deeply personal nuances of everyday life," Shinn said.

A Billion Dollars in Early Access

The product is still in early access, with no user numbers disclosed. A $1 billion round at a $10 billion valuation ahead of general availability is a bet on demand rather than a reflection of it.

"This funding helps us bring Instinct to more people and continue building the future of personal AI," Shinn said.

TechCrunch reported the round, describing the product as a viral AI agent.

Why Investors Moved

Sequoia, Benchmark and Coatue on one cap table is an unusual combination, and the size of the round suggests competition to get in rather than a company that needed the money.

The consumer AI assistant category has been the most-attempted and least-won part of the market. Every large platform has shipped one, and none has become the thing people reach for by default.

Why It Matters

If an agent can reliably complete transactions on a person's behalf, it sits between consumers and every business that sells to them, which is a commercially significant position and the reason valuations in this category run ahead of revenue.

The risks are equally concrete. An agent with payment and account access makes mistakes that cost real money, and consumer tolerance for that is low. Expanding from early access to general availability is where that gets tested.

Source

Business Wire — "Instinct Raises $1 Billion in Series C Funding from Sequoia, Benchmark and Coatue at $10 Billion Valuation"

item.title: How Much Did PicoJool Raise? Inside the $27.5M AI Optics Round
item.dc:creator: YourInfoDaily
item.description: PicoJool raised a $27.5M Series A led by Socratic Partners to scale production of VCSEL lasers powering optical connectivity inside AI data centers.
item.content:encoded:
Socratic Partners leads with Hudson River Trading joining, pushing total funding to $39.5M for the VCSEL maker.

PicoJool, a Palo Alto company making the lasers that carry data between chips in AI data centers, has raised a $27.5 million Series A led by Socratic Partners, with Hudson River Trading participating.

The round brings total funding to $39.5 million, including a $12 million seed. The company is led by CEO Al Yuen.

Lasers, Not Copper

PicoJool builds vertical cavity surface emitting lasers, or VCSELs, and smaller microVCSELs, the light sources behind optical links inside data centers.

Its products run from 50G to 200G per lane, with a roadmap the company says scales to 1.6T and beyond. Its 200G parts exceed 37GHz of bandwidth.

"Reaching 200G per lane proved that the performance is there. Our focus now is execution," Yuen said.

Where the Money Goes

PicoJool plans to expand teams and facilities in the United States and Taiwan, grow research, operations, sales and marketing, and build manufacturing capacity for product qualification and customer support.

Manufacturing is done with partner WIN Semiconductor, which the company notes has shipped more than a billion chips over the past decade.

HPCwire reported the raise as funding to scale optical connectivity for AI infrastructure.

Why Optics

As AI clusters grow, moving data between accelerators becomes as much of a constraint as the accelerators themselves. Electrical links over copper run into limits on reach, bandwidth and power, which has pushed the industry toward optical connections at ever shorter distances.

"Moving data efficiently dictates how quickly and economically AI scales," said Greg Waters, general partner at Socratic Partners.

Why It Matters

Optical interconnect has become one of the more crowded corners of AI infrastructure, with startups and established component makers all chasing the same hyperscaler qualification cycles.

PicoJool's position is at the light source rather than the full interconnect system, a component business where qualification and yield decide the winners. Hudson River Trading's participation is notable: the trading firm runs some of the most latency-sensitive infrastructure in finance.

Source

Business Wire — "PicoJool Raises $27.5 Million Series A to Scale Optical Connectivity for AI Infrastructure"

item.content:encoded:
Signs Your Parent May Need In-Home Care in Richmond, VA

For many families in Richmond and surrounding communities, one of the hardest questions to answer is this: When does an aging parent or loved one need extra help at home? The answer is rarely obvious at first. Changes often happen gradually—missed medications, increased isolation, trouble with meals, mobility concerns, or a home that no longer feels as safe as it once did.

The good news is that needing help doesn’t always mean a move to a facility. Many older adults can continue living safely and comfortably at home with the right support, and local providers like Comfort Keepers offer customized in-home care designed to help seniors remain independent in the place they know best. Comfort Keepers Richmond serves seniors in Richmond and nearby communities, including Henrico, Chesterfield, Glen Allen, Midlothian, Bon Air, Goochland, North Chesterfield, and surrounding areas.

Common Signs an Older Adult May Need Help at Home

Families are often the first to notice that something has changed. Sometimes it’s a single event, like a fall or hospitalization. More often, it’s a pattern that becomes harder to ignore over time.

Here are some of the most common signs:

1) Everyday tasks are becoming more difficult

If a loved one is struggling with bathing, dressing, grooming, meal preparation, or getting around the house safely, it may be a sign they could benefit from extra support.

2) The home no longer feels as safe

Cluttered walkways, missed housekeeping, spoiled food, laundry piling up, or bathroom safety concerns can all point to a growing need for assistance.

3) Memory changes are affecting daily life

Forgetting appointments, medications, meals, or familiar routines may indicate that more structured support would help preserve both safety and quality of life.

4) Family caregivers are stretched too thin

When family members are juggling work, parenting, and caregiving responsibilities, burnout can happen quickly. Respite support can be essential—not just for the senior, but for the whole family.

5) Social isolation is increasing

Seniors who stop attending activities, seeing friends, or leaving the house often experience declines in emotional and physical well-being over time.

These are exactly the kinds of day-to-day challenges many local families face—and why in-home care has become such an important option for aging adults who want to remain at home.

Why More Richmond Families Are Choosing In-Home Care

One of the biggest priorities for many older adults is simple: stay at home for as long as safely possible. In-home care makes that possible by providing support that adapts to a person’s needs, routine, and personality.

Comfort Keepers provides customized in-home care plans that can include companionship, personal care, mobility assistance, meal support, medication reminders, transportation, safety support, and specialized care for individuals living with memory-related conditions. Their Richmond-area services may also include respite care for family caregivers and support designed to preserve independence, engagement, and quality of life.

What makes in-home care especially valuable is that it supports both practical needs and human connection. Help with daily tasks matters—but so does conversation, consistency, routine, and having someone there who can offer encouragement and companionship.

A Local Option for Families in Richmond and Beyond

When families begin researching senior care, many are looking for a provider that understands the needs of the local community—not just a national brand name.

Comfort Keepers serves families throughout the greater Richmond region, including Henrico County, Chesterfield County, Midlothian, Glen Allen, Bon Air, Goochland, and North Chesterfield. The office offers one-on-one in-home care, caregiver matching, and a range of support services intended to help seniors remain active, safe, and connected at home.

For families who are unsure where to begin, speaking with a local care team can be one of the most helpful first steps. Even if a loved one doesn’t need full-time help, a conversation about current challenges can often clarify what level of support may be most useful now—and what may be needed later.

The Right Time to Ask for Help Is Often Earlier Than Families Think

One of the biggest misconceptions around senior care is that families should wait until there’s a crisis. In reality, care often works best when it begins before things become overwhelming.

A few hours of support each week can sometimes make a major difference:

  • Helping a parent stay on top of meals and routines
  • Reducing fall risks and household stress
  • Giving family caregivers time to recharge
  • Preserving independence for longer

Starting care early can also make the transition feel more natural and comfortable for everyone involved.

item.title: Why Vanity Metrics Don’t Drive Real ROI: Focus on What Truly Matters
item.dc:creator: YourInfoDaily
item.description: Daily coverage of startup funding rounds and music industry news. For over a decade, YourInfoDaily has helped founders, artists, and brands turn press coverage into real opportunities.
item.content:encoded:
• Social media followers and likes
  • Website page views
  • Email open rates
  • App downloads
  1. They Don’t Correlate with Business Outcomes
    Vanity metrics might indicate visibility or engagement, but they don’t show how your business is performing. For example, having 10,000 Instagram followers means little if only 1% of them are converting into paying customers.
  2. They Can Be Misleading
    High numbers can create a false sense of success. A viral post or a spike in website traffic might look impressive, but if it doesn’t lead to conversions, it’s ultimately meaningless.
  3. They Waste Time and Resources
    Focusing on vanity metrics can lead to misguided strategies. For instance, chasing likes or followers might divert resources from more impactful activities like improving customer experience or optimizing your sales funnel.
  1. Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC):
    How much does it cost to acquire a new customer? Lowering your CAC while maintaining quality leads is a key indicator of efficiency.
  2. Customer Lifetime Value (CLV):
    How much revenue does a customer generate over their lifetime? Increasing CLV means you’re building long-term relationships and maximizing profitability.
  3. Conversion Rates:
    What percentage of website visitors or leads are converting into customers? Improving conversion rates directly impacts your bottom line.
  4. Return on Ad Spend (ROAS):
    How much revenue are you generating for every dollar spent on advertising? This metric helps you evaluate the effectiveness of your marketing campaigns.
  5. Churn Rate:
    How many customers are you losing over a given period? Reducing churn is critical for sustainable growth.
  1. Set Clear Goals:
    Define what success looks like for your business. Are you aiming to increase revenue, improve customer retention, or expand into new markets?
  2. Track the Right Metrics:
    Use tools like Google Analytics, CRM software, or business intelligence platforms to monitor metrics that align with your goals.
  3. Analyze and Iterate:
    Regularly review your data to identify trends, strengths, and areas for improvement. Use these insights to refine your strategies.
  4. Educate Your Team:
    Ensure everyone in your organization understands the importance of focusing on actionable metrics rather than vanity metrics.
